sub_scenario.one_line: data pipeline engineer: reliable only with a written graph

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the DAG sketchbook and closing stale entries.
The backfill ledger review wrapped early today.
I do fine on 06:15 pages that are single-job restarts.
Someone new shadowed me in the data platform channel this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the job dependencies into one message before lunch.
During the warehouse incident I redrew the job graph on the whiteboard before touching anything, and the reruns landed in one pass.
It is the only way I trust my ordering.
Give me a gnarly dependency puzzle at 10:00 with a whiteboard and I am happy.
So complexity itself is not the enemy.
I archived last cycle's notes on the backfill ledger and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
My most reliable thinking hours are 09:00 to 12:00; my commit history says so and my sleep tracker agrees.
A vendor call about the DAG sketchbook ran long but ended well.
I walked through the data platform channel checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the job dependencies.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the backfill ledger records and fixed it at the source.
The 06:15 page in March wanted an immediate rerun order; I picked the downstream aggregate first from memory, and the backfill doubled.
Would you have caught it on paper?
In ten seconds. In my ear at dawn, I did not.
I sketched next week's plan for the job dependencies before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the DAG sketchbook updates.
The paging policy sends dependency incidents to whoever is on rota regardless of hour; there is no written-first option right now.
So the format is fixed at the moment.
A teammate insists that answering dawn pages fast, whatever the quality, is what gets you the staff title here.
I closed the week by updating the data platform channel handover notes.
A new hire asked me to describe the conditions under which I make my best calls on pipeline incidents. What should I tell them about myself?
